How a rate is set

No pool formula. No utilisation curve. Just bids.

Lending pools set your rate from a spreadsheet curve. Citrine lets lenders compete for every single loan, so the price of credit is whatever the market will actually pay.

01

Lock collateral, name your ceiling

Choose MON, tWETH or tWBTC, the tUSDC you need, a term from five minutes to a year, and the highest APR you would accept. Collateral goes into the exchange contract, not to a person.

02

Lenders bid the rate down

Each bid must beat the last by at least 0.05%. The best bidder's tUSDC sits in escrow; anyone outbid gets theirs back. Late bids extend the clock, so nobody wins by sniping.

03

Accept, or let the clock settle it

Take the best bid whenever you like, or let the auction end and anyone can settle it. tUSDC lands in your wallet in the same block on Monad.

04

The loan becomes a tradable position

The lender receives an ERC-721 that carries the right to be repaid. List it at any price, and a buyer steps into the loan before it matures.

The yield curve, from real loans

Every bar is a clearing price someone actually paid.

Rates grouped by loan term, rebuilt from contract events as they land. Short loans and long loans price differently, and you can see it.

Exit before maturity

Lending without the lock-up.

When a loan funds, the lender is minted a position NFT with its artwork drawn fully onchain. Repayment goes to whoever holds it. Need your tUSDC back early? List the position, and the Trade desk shows buyers its exact yield to maturity.

  • Artwork and terms read straight from tokenURI on the exchange contract
  • Liquidatable when debt reaches 85% of collateral value, priced by Pyth
  • If the borrower misses maturity plus grace, the holder claims the collateral
